classification.difficultyReason: Two-stage chain: find the tower height with tan42°, then use it in tan⁻¹ from the closer point, with minutes.

content.prompt:
From a point $B$ on level ground, 36 m from the base $D$ of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top $A$ is $42^\circ$. Point $C$ lies on $BD$, 15 m from $D$.
Calculate the angle of elevation $\theta$ of $A$ from $C$. Answer to the nearest minute.

answer.worked:
First find the height $AD$ using triangle $ABD$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan42^\circ&=\frac{AD}{36}\\AD&=36\tan42^\circ\\AD&\approx32.41\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Then use triangle $ACD$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{AD}{15}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{36\tan42^\circ}{15}\right)\\\theta&\approx65^\circ10'\end{align*}$$
